messages:
kevin: Heads-up — ACME go-live Sat 03:00 UTC. I started a short runbook draft for prefill/batching/streaming + circuit breakers. Pulling in @maria (CS lead), @jake (solutions), @sara (PM).

maria: Great — can we keep it lean? CS needs clear 'if X then Y' actions.

jake: +1. For large tenants we do: 1) prefill first 100 requests 2) enable streaming for interactive flows 3) fallback to small model if latency spike.

sara: Important: renewal-risk account, so minimize errors. Add a customer-visible grace message for streaming hiccups.

maria: Draft checklist I propose: 
- Confirm prefill keys and sample prompts with engineering by T-6h
- Set client-side retry jitter: base 300ms, max 3s
- Enable KV prefill for top 10 prefixes
- Circuit breaker: fail to cached response after 2 consecutive timeouts >500ms
- Switch to cached-mode (no live generation) if 10% error rate over 1m

kevin: Adding a small config snippet to share with SEs (client-side):
```json
{"prefill": {"enabled": true, "ttl_s": 3600, "batch_size": 50}, "retry": {"base_ms": 300, "max_ms": 3000, "max_attempts": 3}}
```

jake: For server-side policies we should have: autoscale burst to +2 GPUs for 15m OR fallback to lower-capacity region. Also recommend quantized variant for low-priority background calls.

maria: On the customer-facing side, here's a short message to put in their onboarding doc: "If responses slow or stop, we'll automatically serve a cached fallback while we spin up capacity. You can opt out by setting liveFallback=false."

sara: Love that. Also capture feedback: run a small eval set (10 prompts) at T-4h and T-30m; record latency and quality. If quality delta > 3 points, trigger rollback.

kevin: Who's owning the T-6h prefill execution? @maria?

maria: I'll coordinate with the SE on keys and prefills. @jake can run the eval scripts.

jake: Yep — I'll push an eval run and post results to this thread. Script snippet: 
```bash
python tools/eval_latency.py --tenant acme --count 10 --out results/acme_t6.json
```

deploy-bot: deploy started for prefills (job id: pf-7821).

maria: If deploy-bot shows repeated job failures, flip the circuit breaker: set client-side to cached-only and open a support ticket.

kevin: Decision matrix in runbook (short): 
- Latency < 300ms and error <1% => normal ops
- Latency 300-800ms or errors 1-5% => enable reduced batching (batch_size=20), toggle streaming to OPTIMISTIC mode
- Latency >800ms or errors >5% => cached-only + notify customer + escalate to infra oncall

sara: Add a renewal note: if we see >3 incidents in 72h, schedule a renewal-risk cadence call.

jake: Capturing telemetry points to include in postmortem: p50/p95 latency, error rate, prefill success rate, model fallback count, customer-visible fallbacks.

maria: I'll create a quick checklist card in Notion and share link here after T-5h.

kevin: Perfect. @deploy-bot keep us posted. Everyone else — callouts?

sara: One more: plan for manual rollback of model version in 10m window if quality regresses.

jake: I'll add the rollback command to the runbook: 
```bash
redwood rollback --tenant acme --model rdl-v2 --to rdl-v1
```

deploy-bot: prefill job pf-7821 completed successfully in 42s.

maria: Nice. @jake please post eval results when ready.

jake: Results uploaded: p50=120ms, p95=410ms, quality delta=0.5 (no rollback). Posting attachments to Notion.

kevin: Thanks team — I'll lock the runbook, push to customer Slack channel, and schedule a 1hr follow-up at T+2h. :thumbsup:
